summary: All 4 acceptance criteria met. The implementation correctly adds _check_results() and modifies _chain_groups() to propagate stage failures. Only pipeline.py was modified; tasks.py and test_pipeline.py remain unchanged.

checks.detail: POISON_PILL triggers extract_item to raise StageError → _run_group catches it as error dict → _check_results detects it and raises StageError('Stage \'extract\' had 1 failure(s): ...'). Error correctly propagates.
Mixed input: POISON_PILL produces error dict, item_1 produces ok result → _check_results finds 1 error → raises StageError. Partial failure correctly propagates.
All 7 items pass through extract → transform → load successfully. No error dicts → _check_results never raises → returns final stage results with all 'ok' status.

All 4 tests pass: test_success_path_returns_all_results, test_stage1_failure_propagates, test_stage1_failure_not_swallowed, test_error_position_is_detected. Confirmed by executor and verified by code logic analysis.

_check_results.notes: Matches spec with a defensive isinstance(r, dict) guard, which is an acceptable robustness improvement.

_chain_groups.notes: _check_results called after each of the 3 stages (extract, transform, load) exactly as specified.

_run_group.notes: Unchanged — the catch-and-store pattern is intentionally preserved per spec.
